groups.text: A logging helper has to take every list.
A list of payment ids.
A list of amounts in cents.
It never needs to know the element type.
Kotlin says that with a star projection: logAll takes a List of star, and both lists fit.
Read List of star as a list of one specific type, and you don't know which.
Here star points at the list of ids, but the compiler only knows it is a list of something.
It could be the list of ints.
Reading is safe.
Whatever the list holds, each element comes out typed as nullable Any, which fits anything.
Writing is not safe.
star might be the list of ints, so no String may go in.
Kotlin doesn't even let null in, because the unknown type might be non-nullable.
Everything that doesn't take an element still works: size, isEmpty, removeAt and clear.
So a function that empties any buffer can take a MutableList of star.
Java writes the same idea as List of question mark, the unbounded wildcard.
Each element comes out as an Object.
A String can't go in on either side.
Java is more relaxed about null: add(null) compiles on a List of question mark, because every Java reference type allows null.
What the star stands for depends on the declaration.
Take Source, declared out T, with the bound Number.
A Source of star might be a Source of Int, or a Source of BigDecimal.
Whichever it is, next returns some Number.
So reads keep the bound: Source of star means Source of out Number.
Now take Sink, declared in T.
A Sink of star might be a Sink of String, or a Sink of CardAuthorized.
A String fits only the first.
A card authorization fits only the second.
No value is accepted by every one of them, so the compiler allows none.
Nothing is Kotlin's name for a type with no values.
Sink of star means Sink of in Nothing.
So a star is shorthand for the safest projection the declaration allows.
An invariant Box gets both rules.
A Box of star reads as Box of out nullable Any, and writes as Box of in Nothing.
Assign to its item, and the compiler names the type it wanted: Nothing.
Java's question mark follows the same rules: the bound survives it, and a String can't go into a Sink of question mark.
Only null gets through, and only in Java.
